title: VPC: subnets, ranges, and why the network is global

videos.script: In Google Cloud, a network is global. One network, in every region at once. {{global}} It has no address range of its own. The ranges belong to subnets, and a subnet covers one region, every zone of it. {{subnets}} So a machine in São Paulo and one in Santiago can share a network and talk on internal addresses, with nothing in between to build. {{between}} Now the default. Ask gcloud, or Terraform, for a network with only a name, and you get auto mode: a subnet in every region, from one fixed block. {{auto}} Every auto mode network has the same ranges. That is why two of them can never be joined. {{same}} So the planner writes its network in custom mode, region by region. {{custom}} Ranges are the one choice that is expensive to change. A range can grow, never shrink, and two subnets may not overlap. {{rules}} Terraform does not check that last rule. Google does, at apply time, too late. So you check it on your laptop first, with a short program. {{end}}
